title: Subak Water Temples
summary: Modelled on Bali's subak irrigation, where a network of water temples coordinates the rice terraces. The shared resource (here compute and tokens) flows down from the Lake Temple through regional and local temples to the farming agents. Temples share planting schedules with their neighbours, so neighbouring fields work in step and the whole valley avoids clashes: pests in the rice, conflicts among agents.
whenToUse: Many teams share one scarce resource (a GPU, a rate limit, the user's attention) and must time their work so they do not all draw at once.
strengths: Fair sharing of a scarce resource
Neighbours in step avoid clashes; staggered regions avoid peaks
risks: A broken channel starves everything downstream
The calendar is slow to change
Depends on upstream temples sharing fairly

smileMetrics.cooperation: Water (budget) reaching the last terrace ÷ water released.

communication: Budget flows down once per season. Temples at the same level exchange schedules each round. Farmers speak only to their subak temple.
cooperation: Cooperation = budget reaching farms ÷ budget released, times the share of neighbours in step.
